item.title: Python 3.15.2, 3.14.10, 3.13.18, 3.12.16 and 3.11.18 are out
item.description: Five expedited security releases to distrust the compromised eMudhra intermediate CA keys.
item.dc:creator: Hugo van Kemenade

item.title: Python 3.15.1, 3.14.9 and 3.13.17 are out
item.description: Three certified security releases for 3.15, 3.14 and 3.13.
item.dc:creator: Hugo van Kemenade

item.title: Python 3.16.0 alpha 1 is now available
item.description: The first developer preview of Python 3.16 is ready for testing.
item.dc:creator: Savannah Ostrowski

item.title: Python 3.15.0 (final) is here!
item.description: A brand new Python here for you to enjoy!
item.dc:creator: Hugo van Kemenade

item.title: Python 3.10.22, 3.11.17, 3.12.15, 3.13.16 and 3.14.8 are now available!
item.description: Security updates across Python 3.10–3.14, the final maintenance release of 3.13, and a farewell to Python 3.10.
item.dc:creator: Pablo Galindo

item.title: Python Language Summit 2026
item.description: The 2026 Python Language Summit was hosted in Kraków, Poland as part of EuroPython 2026. There were 15 talks covering free-threading, Rust, garbage collection, type annotations, and more.
item.dc:creator: Seth Larson

item.title: Lightning Talks (Python Language Summit 2026)
item.description: Lightning talks on a one-time ABI break, safer interruptions, EktuPy (Scratch but Python), an AGENTS.md file for CPython, and a call to read PEP 836.
item.dc:creator: Seth Larson

item.title: PEP 827: Type Manipulation (Python Language Summit 2026)
item.description: Michael J. Sullivan presents PEP 827 and discusses a key design decision: how to store type annotations?
item.dc:creator: Seth Larson

item.title: Free-Threaded Python Post-Era (Python Language Summit 2026)
item.description: Tobias Wrigstad, Fridtjof Stoldt, and Donghee Na propose a safe and performant, high-level concurrency model for free-threaded Python
item.dc:creator: Seth Larson
